newsitem.title: UK: High yields boost UK wheat/barley crops - Dalgety.
newsitem.headline: High yields boost UK wheat/barley crops - Dalgety.

text.p: High yields have increased the size of British wheat and barley crops, food and agri business group Dalgety Plc said.
Dalgety estimated the UK's 1996 wheat crop at 15.9 million tonnes, up around 1.6 million from last year, and put the barley crop at 7.98 million tonnes, an increase of 1.0 million tonnes.
Andrew Barnard, UK arable crop marketing manager for Dalgety Agriculture ,told a news conferance on Thursday the higher outputs reflected increased yields.

Barnard said the rise in wheat yields was mainly as a result of increases in the all-important Eastern region which achieved 8.11 tonnes per hectare -- a gain of 0.2 tonnes per hectre over last year's result.

The national average wheat yield from Dalgety's survey of 1,000 farmers was 8.23 tonnes per hectare which had created a new record, beating the 1984 yield 7.71 tonnes. With a total consumption figure of 12.1 million tonnes Barnard said the UK would have an exportable wheat balance of 4.65 million.

Higher barley output was due to both area increases and new varities of winter barleys being allowed to develop to their full yield potential. Barnard forecast barley imports of 0.15 million tonnes indicating a surplus for export or intervention of 2.11 million tonnes.
